name: Careers in Food Science

objectives.text: Identify jobs that people do to grow, process, inspect, and sell food
Describe how people in food careers help keep food safe, healthy, and available for families and communities
Describe the daily work of a food scientist, food inspector, or dietitian
Compare the tools, workplaces, and tasks of food careers in laboratories, processing plants, and commercial kitchens
Investigate the education, certifications, and skills required for a career in food science or food safety
Explain how school subjects such as chemistry, biology, and math are used on the job by food science professionals
Analyze career pathways available in food production, processing, quality control, and product development
Explain the role of quality assurance and food safety professionals and the purpose of the tests they perform on food products
Describe how research and development food scientists apply biochemistry to create new and value added food products
Explain how FFA Career Development Events such as Food Science and Technology and Meats Evaluation build competencies used in food industry careers
Design a supervised agricultural experience plan that builds skills toward a chosen food science career
Compare the roles of food science professionals working in government regulatory agencies, private industry, and university research and extension
Analyze labor market information such as salary ranges, job demand, and regional employers for food science careers
Conduct an informational interview or job shadow with a food industry professional and report on the responsibilities and outlook of the career
Evaluate the qualifications needed for a specific food science career of personal interest against current personal skills and experience
Evaluate how food science professionals serve others through honesty, safety, and stewardship in their daily work
Create a resume and portfolio that document SAE, FFA, and coursework accomplishments for a food science position or scholarship
Formulate a career plan that outlines the education, credentials, and experience needed to enter a chosen food science profession

changes: Kept and lightly reworded all six existing objectives because each names a real career competency. Added grade 4, 6, and 8 objectives to fill gaps on the purpose of food careers, the settings where food professionals work, and how school subjects are used on the job. Added high school objectives on quality assurance and R&D roles, aligned to FPP.01.02.04.a and FPP.02.02.03.a. Also added objectives on FFA CDE connections, SAE planning, comparing government, industry, and academic roles, labor market analysis, informational interviews and job shadowing, vocational ethics, and a resume and portfolio. The other candidate standards cover product development, packaging, and distribution content that belongs to sibling sub-topics, so they were not used.
